Benefits include retirement benefits and PTO.

HiO (hio.ai) | Growth Marketing Manager | Remote (US, Eastern hours) | Full-time | $140K–$160K + equity

HiO is an AI business partner for small business owners. It works across their customer conversations on Instagram, WhatsApp, SMS and email, spots opportunities and flags what needs the owner’s attention. We’ve raised a $16M seed round and we’re a small team that moves fast.

We need our first growth hire, and you’d own the growth engine end to end. That means paid social and search with real budget accountability, SEO and visibility in AI/LLM answers, landing page and signup conversion, referral, and testing new channels and killing the ones that don’t work. You’d also build the measurement layer from scratch: funnel instrumentation, CAC/LTV and activation metrics.

There’s no dedicated growth engineer, so you’ll build your own automation: AI-assisted creative testing, automated reporting and agentic campaign workflows.

What we’re looking for: 5+ years in growth at a SaaS company (SMB or PLG at seed or Series A is ideal). You’ve owned the full funnel yourself rather than executing someone else’s strategy, and you can show specific workflows you’ve automated with AI. This is a hands-on role with no team to manage near-term.

Apply: https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/4468585742/

I'm applying for the Growth Lead / Expansion & Lifecycle role, specifically the expansion + lifecycle automation piece.

Concretely, for the fixed-fee milestone structure:

Milestone 1 (week 1-2): instrument the activation and retention funnel end to end - event taxonomy, tracking, and a dashboard you can actually make decisions from. Deliverable is a written diagnosis with the three highest-leverage lifecycle drops and what each is worth in ARR.

Milestone 2 (week 3-6): build the lifecycle automation itself - onboarding email/nudge sequences, dormant-user winback, and cancellation-save flows, wired to the product so behavior triggers them rather than a manual send.

How I would work: start by reading the existing signup flow and instrumenting before changing anything, so milestone 2 is driven by observed drop-off rather than my assumption of where it is. I would want to agree the milestone boundaries before starting either.

Two questions so I can quote accurately: what is the current activation rate and the trial-to-paid conversion you are working from? And is the fixed fee negotiable against a smaller first milestone if the diagnosis itself is useful?

To be direct about fit: I am proposing scope and milestones rather than claiming a track record I cannot show you here.

Mattermost | Remote (US and Canada) | FT | Multiple roles

Mattermost (https://mattermost.com) is an open-core collaboration and workflow automation platform for air-gapped, on-prem and private clouds. Our customers are in defense, intelligence, security and critical infrastructure, including the USAF and NASA. Y Combinator led our Series B, their largest open-source investment at the time.

Both openings are full stack on the core platform: Go backend, React/TypeScript frontend, PostgreSQL and Redis. The codebase is public (https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost), so most of what you build is too. We would rather hire people who ship and own complex software end to end than chase an exact stack match, so any systems or backend language and any frontend stack counts. What we look for in both roles: REST and WebSocket APIs with real networking fundamentals (HTTP, connection lifecycle), and relational databases including schema design and query optimization.

We use coding agents daily (Claude Code, Cursor, and others) at every stage of the work: planning, building, reviewing, testing, and shipping. We treat that as core craft rather than a shortcut around the fundamentals. If you have a track record of shipping and owning complex software end-to-end, we want to hear from you.

Senior Full Stack Engineer $142,723 - $172,723 USD Architect and ship full stack features end to end, own the testing strategy for what you ship, and build internal tooling and testing infrastructure that makes the rest of the team faster. You will work without close supervision and hold the security and compliance bar our customers require. Nice to have: distributed systems and high availability architecture, regulated-environment security, open-source contributions, experience on remote-first teams.

Join our team: https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/mattermost/jobs/5379251008

Staff Full Stack Engineer $172,724 - $227,135 USD Set technical direction for the platform rather than for a feature area: architecture and roadmap across the stack, the standards for how the org uses coding agents, and the strategy for internal tooling and testing. You will influence direction across teams, partner with security and compliance on it, and mentor senior engineers. Nice to have: staff, principal or tech lead experience elsewhere, open-source maintainership, FedRAMP or ITAR familiarity, defense or critical infrastructure background.

Join our team: https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/mattermost/jobs/5405811008

Both roles have Canadian postings: https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/mattermost

Search Atlas | Product Engineer (Product Manager role, not a Full-stack role) | REMOTE (anywhere, EST hours) | Full-time contractor | $23-$34 USD/hour | https://careers.searchatlas.com/jobs/599248-product-engineer...

We're ~160 people, fully remote, building an AI marketing platform. Our main product is OTTO, which runs a site's SEO on its own - it reads live search data and pushes the technical and on-page fixes itself, nobody queues them up. Around that we've got ad automation for Google and Meta, GBP management for multi-location brands, content gen, and LLM visibility tracking (whether ChatGPT and co are citing you). Autotrader, Hyundai, P&G, Vendasta are some of our customers.

Work happens in pods, 1 PM and 2-4 engineers. You own your pod's roadmap and ship it with them, no veteran PM signing off on your specs first. That's the part most PM roles won't hand you.

Looking for 3+ years PM in B2B SaaS with an actual technical background - eng or QA before PM, or a PM who's been getting into the codebase themselves. You should be able to read Python and TS, write your own SQL, find your way around an API, and not need an engineer to tell you what a stack trace says. We're Django on the back, React/Next on the front. QA is yours end to end including release sign-off, people tend to underestimate that bit. And you're already using Claude Code or similar daily, not "open to it".

A few notes before you apply:

- Experience: we're looking for people with a few years of hands-on product or engineering work behind them. The role is autonomous from the first week, so we need you ready to take the wheel. - Recruiting agencies: we hire in-house and manage every application ourselves, so there's no need to send candidates or reach out about partnerships. Thank you for understanding! - If your stack matches, please do reach out. Django/DRF/Celery/Postgres with React/Next, Python automation work around SEO: if that's your day-to-day and you're using AI coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, whatever you like) in your real workflow, I want to hear from you. Don't talk yourself out of it because the title isn't an exact fit; tell me what you've built.

Recruitment process is screen with me, a take-home that runs about 75 mins, technical round with one of our senior PMs, then a call with our Director of Product (who you'd report to). I usually come back to people within 2 business days.

Our ATS forces us to list specific ywhere as long as you can do EST hours, so apply even if yours isn't

Apply at the link and mention HN somewhere, in your pitch or wherever it fits. joao.pedro@searchatlas.com if you need me, though the link's faster.

P.S: Not a PM, or the PM role isn't quite your thing? Have a look at everything else we have open at https://careers.searchatlas.com and apply directly to the role that suits you best (preferred route). If you're not sure which one that is, email me with a short line on what you do and I'll point you to the right one.

Workday | AI Creative Technologist | Pleasanton, CA | ONSITE | Contract

Workday's in-house creative team already uses AI every day. We built our own agent platform (Creative AI Studio) and now need a hands-on technologist to keep it running well and build what comes next.

Half the work is building: new role-specific agents, plus integrations and automations over APIs and MCP servers that move work from request to brief to production to review with fewer manual handoffs. The other half is making shipped tools work for people: supporting users, improving agents through PRs, and teaching designers and writers to get real value from them. You'll also be our technical filter on AI vendors, looking past the demo to the architecture, security, data handling, and pricing.

You'd be a good fit if you: - Have shipped AI agents or agentic workflows that real users depend on (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) - Are at home in a repo: branches, PRs, code review, release hygiene - Understand APIs, auth, webhooks, and MCP, and can map data flows before you build - Can teach a room of non-technical creatives without jargon

Not a fit if you want to build but not support or teach, or you'd rather research AI than ship it.

To apply, email chris.varela@workday.com with your resume and links or write-ups for one or two things you've built. For each one, tell me what problem it solved, how it works, and what you'd change now. I'm the hiring manager and read every one.

Workday's in-house creative team already uses AI every day. We built our own agent platform (Creative AI Studio) and now need a hands-on technologist to keep it running well and build what comes next.

Half the work is building: new role-specific agents, plus integrations and automations over APIs and MCP servers that move work from request to brief to production to review with fewer manual handoffs. The other half is making shipped tools work for people: supporting users, improving agents through PRs, and teaching designers and writers to get real value from them. You'll also be our technical filter on AI vendors, looking past the demo to the architecture, security, data handling, and pricing.

You'd be a good fit if you: - Have shipped AI agents or agentic workflows that real users depend on (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) - Are at home in a repo: branches, PRs, code review, release hygiene - Understand APIs, auth, webhooks, and MCP, and can map data flows before you build - Can teach a room of non-technical creatives without jargon

Not a fit if you want to build but not support or teach, or you'd rather research AI than ship it.

To apply, email chris.varela@workday.com with your resume and links or write-ups for one or two things you've built. For each one, tell me what problem it solved, how it works, and what you'd change now. I'm the hiring manager and read every one.

QUOBYTE | Santa Clara, CA and Berlin, Germany | Full-time / Remote | ONSITE | https://www.quobyte.com/

At Quobyte we are working on a highly scalable and fault-tolerant software storage system built around a parallel file system core. Our customers use us for large scale AI and HPC clusters in the enterprise and research, k8s and OpenStack infrastructures, and as a scalable backend for SaaS products. There are Quobyte clusters which span tens of thousands of machines and slurp 100s of GB/s!

Under the hood, we have built a full-stack fault-tolerant parallel file system, with everything from kernel development over our own replicated database system design to distributed algorithms (Paxos!) and performance. In short: lots of real-world challenging and fun problems!

We work as a highly efficient engineering team, ship frequently, do code reviews, and have lots of unit and integration testing. If you’re passionate about systems, we might be the right place for you!

Berlin, Germany (onsite, please apply only if you already are in the EU):

* Software Engineer (with a passion for Systems, 60-100k EUR)

* QA Engineer (creative testing, test automation, release engineering, 60-100k EUR)

* Infrastructure Engineer (engineering and corporate infrastructure, 50-90k)

* Customer Success Engineer (50-90k)

For detailed job descriptions please and application process, please visit https://www.quobyte.com/company/careers or write to work at quobyte.com.

Sidekick Labs | Senior SWE, R&D Engineer, Intelligence Engineer | REMOTE (US Timezones) | Full-time | $170k to $230k Base + Equity + Health

Sidekick builds AI security software for enterprises. Our sensors observe AI behavior and use in situ. From those observations, our reasoning pipeline produces an application inventory and a risk picture, allowing us to provide real-time intervention and coaching right when it matters.

Compensation: base salary scaled to experience, meaningful early-stage equity, and 100% covered health insurance for you and your immediate family

We are a highly senior team. Most of us have been founders or on early founding teams, so we operate with high ownership. We expect you to have a real, current AI-assisted development practice. Our system spans several languages, and we expect you to use AI tools to quickly navigate unfamiliar parts of the codebase so you can comfortably own problems end-to-end across a broad stack.

We are hiring for three roles:

- Senior Software Engineer: You will work across our event-driven architecture. You'll write Go and Python backend services and touch endpoint-deployed browser and desktop components. You need to be comfortable developing in a multi-tenant, microservice-driven SaaS architecture and understand typical scale and security implications for such products.

- R&D Engineer: This is not an open-ended research function. You will take ambiguous feasibility questions tied to our roadmap and return defensible answers inside a week. You'll build handoff-ready prototypes, then shift into engineering mode to personally drive them through to production. You will also define operational envelopes and degradation boundaries, and rigorously deprecate infeasible ideas with documented rationale to avoid future re-litigation.

- Intelligence and Data Processing Engineer: This role is for someone who loves real browser and desktop forensics. You'll use dev tools and debuggers as your primary instruments. Expect to be reading minified code to find where state lives and analyzing network logs to understand undocumented APIs. You will figure out how AI products work and build the prototyping and automation to maintain our software inventory.

To apply: Send an email to eric+hn@sidekicklabs.com with the role in the subject. Include a PDF of your resume, a quick sentence or two about a tough technical problem you've solved recently, and links to your GitHub, personal site, and/or LinkedIn.

I'm Eric, VP of Technology, and I will personally read every email sent to the HN subaddress. You can view my background here: https://www.linkedin.com/in/three-two-one

https://sidekicklabs.com

InfoHawk | Software Engineer | London, UK or NYC | HYBRID (UK or US), occasional onsite | Full-time | https://www.infohawk.com

Fraud reaches people through ads, cloned brand sites, counterfeit shops and AI-generated video, and it moves faster than any manual review. InfoHawk detects it while it is still running, correlates it across platforms and formats, and surfaces it early enough for our customers to act. We are a small team of engineers plus security, privacy and fraud specialists. Pre-seed, $2.25M led by Moonshots Capital: https://www.infohawk.com/news/2026-06-08-pre-seed-funding-an...

You’d own how data gets in: scrapers and collectors that survive source changes, official APIs where they exist, undocumented endpoints where they don’t. Sources break constantly. Can you figure out how to use AI to spot the change and adapt automatically? Stack: TypeScript, Node, SvelteKit, Postgres, Playwright, heavy AI-assisted development.

We’re looking for ~3-5 years building scraping or integration systems in production, but if you’re a great engineer who doesn’t tick every box we’d still like to hear from you. UK-based for London, US-based for NYC; we cannot sponsor visas. Two of our three founders are engineers, one in each city, and you’ll work with them directly.

james@infohawk.com
